belief: I need a partner to be complete.
origins: Songs, movies, and even sermons can suggest that one is half a person until paired up. After a breakup or in a long single season, loneliness can feel like proof. Some of us have also learned to look to a partner to fill emptiness only God can fill, and that can put an impossible burden on any relationship.
teaches: Paul writes of Christ, “You have been made complete in Christ, who is the head over every ruler and authority.” He says that marriage and singleness are both gifts. The psalmist says, “You have made known to me the path of life; You will fill me with joy in Your presence.” And God promises, “My God will supply all your needs according to His glorious riches in Christ Jesus.” A partner can be a wonderful gift, but no person can complete us. If we expect them to, we set both of us up to be disappointed.
self_statements: I am only half a person alone.
I will not be happy until I have someone.
I cannot cope on my own.
A partner would fix my emptiness.
Being single is a lesser life.
I need someone to be whole.
errors: Believing I am either complete with a partner or incomplete without.
Believing a partner will solve my emptiness.
Feeling lonely and concluding that I am incomplete.
Insisting that I should be partnered by now.
questions: What do I hope a partner would give me, and what does Scripture say about where those needs are met?
Have I seen partnered people who are still unfulfilled?
What strengths do I have that make me whole as I am?
What would it look like to be content and open at the same time?
What does being complete in Christ mean for me?
How can I enjoy life and relationships now?
truth: I am complete in Christ. A partner would be a gift, not a missing piece. I can enjoy my life, build deep friendships, and be open to love without making any person responsible for making me whole.
hw_truths: Marriage and singleness are both gifts.
God fills me with joy in His presence.
I can be whole and open to love.
log: Each week, note one time you felt content or full without a partner.
actions: Write what you want a partner to provide.
Beside each, write how God and friends can meet it.
Invest in a few close relationships.
Ask God to fill you with joy.
prayer: Father, I have looked for someone else to complete me. Thank You that I am complete in Christ. Fill the empty places with Your presence, and prepare me to love well, whether single or married. Amen.
hw_questions: What do I want a partner to give me?
Where else can those needs be met?
What does complete in Christ mean?
How can I be open and content?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I have been made complete in Christ.”
